title: Permissions Lifecycle, Procurement & Travel Guidance (Enterprise Playbook)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates company-wide rules and step-by-step procedures for access and permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement and expenses, vendor engagement, and employee travel. It is intended for requestors, approvers, administrators, and finance partners.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to Redwood systems or acting on Redwood’s financial accounts.
- Intent: Reduce risk, accelerate routine approvals, and centralize templates and routing for consistent auditability.

1) Access & Permissions (Lifecycle)
Overview:
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP) is required for all resources. Access must be justified, time-limited when possible, and reviewed quarterly.
Ownership:
- Resource owners: engineering/product/security teams associated with the application or dataset.
- Access steward: IAM team (eng-infra) maintains role definitions and RBAC groups.
Standards and SLOs:
- Standard access request turnaround: 48 business hours for low-risk requests; 5 business days for elevated access.
- Emergency access (break-glass): logged and reviewed within 24 hours.
Request workflow (summary):
1. Requestor files request via Access Portal (Jira Service Desk form: "Access Request").
2. Requestor selects resource owner, justification, and duration.
3. Resource owner approves/denies. If approved and sensitive scope, Security reviews before IAM grants.
4. IAM provisions and annotates the ticket with grant artifact.
5. Access is automatically expired if a TTL was set; otherwise flagged for quarterly review.
RBAC example (reference role YAML):
```yaml
role: data-analyst-readonly
bindings:
  - group: analytics-readers@redwood.example.com
  - resources: bucket:analytics-prod/*
  - permissions:
      - s3:GetObject
      - s3:ListBucket
ttl_days: 90
approval_required: true
```
Quarterly review checklist (owners):
- Export current group membership for each sensitive role.
- Confirm active members have active justification; remove stale entries.
- Record review in the Access Portal with reviewer name and timestamp.

2) Change Management (Production & Infra)
Policy summary:
- All changes that modify production behaviour, infra networking, or data schemas must follow the Change Workflow. Low-risk changes may use the expedited channel with pre-approved change templates.
Change classification:
- Standard (low risk): Documentation updates, non-prod config changes.
- Significant (medium risk): Service config, feature flags impacting >5% of traffic, schema migrations with rollbacks.
- High-risk: Network changes, infra scaling affecting capacity, security patching with potential restart windows.
Change procedure (detailed steps):
1. Create Change Request (CR) in the Change Board queue with owner, impact analysis, rollback plan, and runbook reference.
2. Automated pre-checks run (CI tests, lint, policy scans).
3. For Significant/High-risk changes, notify SRE and Security at least 48 hours before implementation.
4. Approvals: owner + SRE (for production impact) + Security (if data/security relevance) + Product for user-visible changes.
5. Schedule a maintenance window if needed and communicate to stakeholders.
6. Execute with runbook, monitor metrics and distributed tracing.
7. Rollback if error budget or alert thresholds breached; create post-change note with outcomes.
Runbook requirements (minimum):
- Pre-checks, exact CLI commands, expected outputs, verification queries, rollback commands, and post-mortem owner.
Verification metrics and thresholds:
- Error rate increment > 2x baseline or latency increase > 50th percentile by 200ms triggers rollback.

3) Data Management & Classification
Data classification levels:
- Public (P): safe to publish.
- Internal (I): internal use, non-sensitive.
- Confidential (C): PII, customer data, or regulated content.
- Restricted (R): Cryptographic keys, HSM materials, or legally protected datasets.
Handling rules per classification (summary):
- Encryption at rest and in transit for C and R.
- Access logged and restricted to audited groups.
- Data retention and deletion schedules defined in the data catalog.
- Data sharing with third parties requires a DPA and Security sign-off.
Data lifecycle example (table-like):
- Ingest -> Catalog -> Classify -> Apply Policy (encryption, retention) -> Access Review -> Archive/Delete
Data breach response (summary steps):
1. Notify Incident Response (security).
2. Contain: revoke access, isolate storage.
3. Assess scope and notify legal.
4. Notify affected customers/authorities per regulatory timelines.

4) Procurement & Expenses (Approval Matrix and Templates)
Procurement thresholds (approval matrix):
- Up to $1,000: Team manager approval.
- $1,001 - $25,000: Department head + Finance lead.
- $25,001 - $250,000: VP-level approval + Procurement committee review.
- > $250,000: Executive approval + Legal review (contract required).
Vendor selection rules:
- Competitive bidding required for purchases > $25,000 (minimum 3 bids) unless sole-source justification provided.
- Preferred vendors lists maintained by Procurement (Finance).
Expense policy highlights:
- Domestic travel: per diem capped at $120/day; receipts required for single items > $75.
- International travel: higher per diem; pre-approval required.
- Card usage: Company cards may be used for approved business expenses; card holder training required annually.
Template: Purchase Request (short):
- Requestor: [name]
- Business justification: [text]
- Budget code: [GL account]
- Amount: [USD]
- Vendor: [name]
- Required by: [date]
- Attachments: quote, vendor form, security questionnaire (if SaaS)
Procurement process (steps):
1. Create Purchase Request in Procurement Portal.
2. Attach quote(s) and security questionnaire for SaaS.
3. Manager approves; Procurement verifies vendors and pricing.
4. Finance approves by budget availability.
5. Contracts/Legal review if required; Purchase Order (PO) issued.

5) Vendor Management & Security Questionnaire
Vendor onboarding steps:
1. Complete Vendor Intake form in Procurement Portal (contact, scope, contracts).
2. Vendor completes Security Questionnaire (standard template).
3. Security team reviews answers and assigns risk tier (Low/Medium/High).
4. High-risk vendors require SOC2 or equivalent evidence and a remediation plan.
5. Sign contract with data protection and liability clauses; include SCIM/SAML details if SSO integration.
Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual reviews for medium-risk; quarterly for high-risk.
- Contract expiration alerts generated 90 days prior.

6) Travel and Reimbursement Policy (Concise)
Pre-approval:
- All trips require manager pre-approval in Travel Portal. International travel requires Security brief for certain countries.
Booking:
- Use approved travel vendors (corporate booking link). Fly economy for flights < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
Allowable expenses and caps:
- Meals: up to per diem; receipts recommended.
- Ground transport: rideshare preferred; car rentals require justification.
- Entertainment: must be itemized and have business purpose; additional approvals for amounts > $500.
Reimbursement timeline:
- Submit expenses within 14 days of trip completion. Finance processes reimbursements within 10 business days of submission if complete.
Non-compliance consequences:
- Unapproved expenses may be rejected or reimbursed to the employee at Finance discretion; repeated policy violations escalate to People Ops.

7) Templates & Checklists (Indexed)
Included templates (attachments on portal):
- Access Request form (Jira template ID: AR-2024).
- Change Request template (CR-Standard).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VQ-2.1).
- Purchase Request template (PR-Compact).
- Travel Pre-approval form (TP-Form).
Sample CLI snippets for administrators (reference):
- Grant a Google group membership:
  gcloud identity groups memberships add --group-email=analytics-readers@redwood.example.com --member-email=jane.doe@redwood.example.com
- Revoke AWS S3 access policy (example):
  aws iam detach-user-policy --user-name temporary-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess
Audit and evidence preservation:
- All approvals for access, purchases, and travel must be recorded in their respective portals and retained for 7 years unless legal holds apply.

Governance, exceptions, and escalation:
- Exceptions: Exceptions are allowed only with documented justification and sign-off from the policy owner and an executive sponsor. Exception records are added to the policy exceptions register.
- Escalation: Unresolved approvals beyond SLAs escalate to the functional head then to the Chief of Staff. Security incidents escalate per the Incident Response playbook.
